title: IRCC can’t confirm if Start-Up Visa replacement program details will come this year
html:
Nearly a year after pausing the beleaguered Start-Up Visa program, the Canadian government can’t confirm when it will release details on a proposed replacement pilot program.

The news: In December 2025, the feds suspended applications for Canada’s Start-Up Visa program, meant to be a pathway to citizenship for immigrant founders. At the time, the government said that “more information about the new pilot program for entrepreneurs will be communicated in 2026.”

But in an email to BetaKit on Friday, an IRCC spokesperson said the department is “awaiting a number of key decisions” about the pilot and is “unable to confirm” whether those details will be available before the end of the year.

From the source: While no formal announcement has yet been made about the replacement program, IRCC’s 2026-2027 Departmental Plan includes the following priority: “Creating a new high-impact Start-Up Visa pilot that will replace and address observed issues with the existing Start-Up Visa program, to better support business development and economic growth.” The program and its eligibility will focus on “elite entrepreneurs,” it says.

The context: Originally launched as a five-year pilot program in 2013, replacing the longstanding Federal Entrepreneurship Program, the Start-Up Visa program was meant to attract and retain global entrepreneurial talent to Canada. The SUV offered a direct path to permanent residency for founders hoping to move to Canada, but it was plagued by slow processing times and critics said the program’s design was vulnerable to abuse. By the end of 2025, SUV wait times had ballooned to somewhere between 10 and 35 years, before the program was suspended in anticipation of a new pilot program.

Final thought: In addition to reducing immigration levels, Prime Minister Mark Carney has committed to reducing the public sector workforce, including jobs at IRCC. Last year, IRCC announced it would cut 3,300 roles—or about 25 percent of its workforce—over three years, despite a backlog of immigration applications.

Feature image courtesy Ziyuang Wang via Unsplash.
summary: Feds had previously said they would share details on new pilot program in 2026. The post IRCC can’t confirm if Start-Up Visa replacement program details will come this year first appeared on BetaKit .
